description: Review the architecture of a distributed caching system.
recommendation: All engineering gates passed. Ready for human review and approval.

result.response:
Strengths
- Horizontal scalability via sharding and replication; consistent hashing reduces rebalancing impact.
- Multi-tier caching (local + distributed) lowers latency and offloads hotspots.
- Pluggable eviction (LRU/LFU) and TTLs support diverse workload patterns.
- Write-through/behind options balance latency and durability; quorum reads/writes improve availability.
- Observability hooks (metrics/tracing) and circuit breakers/backpressure protect downstream systems.

Weaknesses
- Potential hot-key amplification despite consistent hashing; limited adaptive load-aware routing.
- Cache invalidation complexity across regions; eventual consistency may cause stale reads.
- Rebalance and failover can trigger thundering herds without coordinated warmup.
- Limited multi-tenant isolation (no per-tenant quotas/priority), risk of noisy neighbors.
- Security posture unclear: data-in-transit/at-rest encryption and authZ granularity may be insufficient.
- Write-behind durability and ordering guarantees under network partitions not fully specified.

Recommendations
1) Introduce adaptive, load-aware key routing and hotspot mitigation (key splitting, request coalescing, server-side batching) with negative cache for miss storms.
2) Strengthen consistency and invalidation: region-aware namespaces, versioned entries, pub/sub with acked fanout, and bounded staleness SLAs; add warmup on rebalance/failover.
3) Enhance isolation and resilience: per-tenant quotas/priority queues, end-to-end mTLS + per-tenant authZ, durable write-behind with WAL and idempotent sinks; embed SLOs with autoscaling and rate-limits tied to hit ratio/latency.
